subject.title: Skipped group messages behind requireMention do not reach message hooks, which blocks full-history archive plugins

question: Should OpenClaw accept a public read-only early inbound observation hook for mention- or policy-skipped messages, and what opt-in/privacy boundary should it have?
rationale: This expands the Plugin SDK and exposes messages that current channel policy skips, so code inspection can show the gap but cannot choose the permanent API/security contract.

options.title: Accept a narrow read-only hook
options.body: Proceed with a minimized inbound_observed-style API that cannot redirect, suppress, reply, or bypass allowlists, and require explicit docs/tests for privacy boundaries.

options.title: Keep only existing ingest behavior
options.body: Reject the new public hook and document that full-fidelity archives require channel-owned ingest config or channel-specific implementations.

options.title: Fold into broader routing hook design
options.body: Defer this issue to the before_route_inbound_message work, accepting a larger and riskier modifying-hook review surface.

recommendation.title: Accept a narrow read-only hook
recommendation.body: Proceed with a minimized inbound_observed-style API that cannot redirect, suppress, reply, or bypass allowlists, and require explicit docs/tests for privacy boundaries.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the shipped partial internal ingest path and are the strongest current-main history signal for this behavior.
